_comment_csp: carries a load-bearing inline script (the beforeinstallprompt catcher — Chrome fires that
event before the React bundle parses, so it MUST be caught in the head; see
src/utils/installPrompt.js) plus four application/ld+json blocks that carry the site's
structured data. Dropping 'unsafe-inline' silently kills the Put-it-on-your-phone button
and the rich search results. A nonce is not available (Vercel serves these as static
files, so there is no per-request server render to inject one), and hashes would have to
be recomputed by hand on every edit — a footgun that breaks the site the first time
someone forgets. The exposure this leaves is XSS-only, and the app has no XSS sink: no
dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere, no eval, no innerHTML, and React escapes all
interpolation. Revisit if any of those three facts stops being true.
